Anhalt was a small German state on the middle Elbe, around Dessau, ruled by the House of Ascania from the 13th century until 1918. In 1815 it was split into three duchies, Anhalt-Dessau, Anhalt-Bernburg and Anhalt-Köthen, all members of the German Confederation. They were reunited as a single Duchy of Anhalt in 1863.

Its princes repeatedly divided their land among heirs, which kept it small and scattered. Yet it had reach: a princess of Anhalt-Zerbst became Catherine the Great of Russia. Prince Leopold III of Anhalt-Dessau laid out the Dessau-Wörlitz garden realm in the late 18th century, an early English-style landscape park.

Anhalt joined the German Empire in 1871 and became a free state after 1918. In 1925 the Bauhaus school moved to Dessau. After 1945 Anhalt was merged into Saxony-Anhalt, in East Germany.
